questions.question: Rutherford’s α-particle scattering experiment on gold foil is responsible for the discovery of which thing?
questions.questionHtml: Rutherford’s α-particle scattering experiment on gold foil is responsible for the discovery of which thing?
questions.solution:
Rutherford’s α-particle scattering experiment on gold foil led to the discovery of the nucleus.

The experiment showed that most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil, indicating atoms are mostly empty space. However, a small fraction of the alpha particles were deflected at large angles or even bounced back, suggesting the existence of a small, dense, positively charged core within the atom. This core was named the nucleus, fundamentally changing the atomic model from the earlier "plum pudding" model to the nuclear model of the atom.

questions.question: From which archaeological site of Indus Valley Civilization, the figures or models of boat are found?
questions.questionHtml: From which archaeological site of Indus Valley Civilization, the figures or models of boat are found?
questions.solution:
The figures or models of boats from the Indus Valley Civilization are found at the archaeological sites of Mohenjodaro and Lothal.

These findings suggest that both sites were involved in trade and transport via waterways, making them key centers for maritime activity.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts placed the disputes relating to election of the president, vice-president, prime minister and Speaker beyond the scope of the judiciary? They are to be decided by such authority as may be determined by the Parliament.
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Amendment Acts placed the disputes relating to election of the president, vice-president, prime minister and Speaker beyond the scope of the judiciary? They are to be decided by such authority as may be determined by the Parliament.
questions.solution:
The Thirty-Ninth Amendment Act, 1975 of the Indian Constitution placed disputes relating to the election of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, and Speaker beyond the scope of the judiciary. According to this amendment, such disputes are to be decided by such authority as may be determined by the Parliament and not by the courts.

This amendment was enacted during the Emergency period and curtailed the powers of the judiciary with respect to electoral disputes involving these highest offices.
